title: field-guide-auditor-walkthroughs-evidence-snapshots
summary: Practical pocket guide for running live auditor walkthroughs and delivering reproducible evidence snapshots for SOC 2 / ISO 27001 controls that depend on RBAC v2 and SIEM exports. Focused on what auditors ask for, where artifacts live, and repeatable sampling and automation approaches.
scope: This doc covers control-to-artifact mapping for common identity, access, and logging controls (principally RBAC v2 enforcement, audit log schema, SIEM export pipeline), a pragmatic sampling strategy for evidence, pre-built synthetic snapshots to speed audits, common gaps we've seen across recent assessments, and a scripted Q&A walkthrough for auditors.
quick_checklist: 1) Prepare evidence snapshot bundle (s3://redwood-evidence/audit-snapshots/<date>). 2) Export RBAC policy snapshot (rbac_v2_policy_export_<date>.json). 3) Generate SIEM sample export (siem_export_sample_<date>.ndjson). 4) Run sample replay to show live pipeline (kitchen: audit-replay job). 5) Confirm KMS audit events and key rotation logs. 6) Share signed hash of bundle with auditor and record delivery in Jira SEC-4123.
control_mapping: High-level mapping: - SOC 2 CC6/ISO A.9 (access control): evidence = RBAC v2 policy export, access review reports, configuration history. - SOC 2 CC7/ISO A.12 (logging & monitoring): evidence = raw audit log NDJSON, SIEM ingestion receipts, SIEM query screenshots, retention policy. - SOC 2 CC5/ISO A.8 (change management): evidence = deploy PRs, audit-runbook timestamps, release tags. For each control we include: artifact name, canonical storage path, last retention purge date, and automated evidence extractor reference (e.g. github.com/org/evidence-collector:main).
sampling_strategy: Proposed two-stage sampling: 1) Deterministic coverage: for each control select the last 90 days and extract one guaranteed artifact per quarter (policy export, access review, key rotation). 2) Stratified random sampling for logs: sample by environment (prod/staging), by user type (svc-account/human/admin), and by event type (authz-grant, token-create, policy-change). Aim for 200 log events per environment for a medium-sized customer. Document sample seeds and random generator used so auditor can reproduce (seed=20241118-audit).
siem_export_examples: We send exports as newline-delimited JSON with a light canonical schema. Example NDJSON event (stringified): {"ts":"2024-11-10T21:07:33Z","event_type":"policy_change","actor":"user:alice@redwood.ai","resource":"cluster/gpu-pool-7","before":"eyJyb2xlcyI6WyJkZWZhdWx0Il19","after":"eyJyb2xlcyI6WyJhZG1pbiJdfQ==","trace_id":"trace-4f2a"}. Also include a SIEM ingest acknowledgement file: siem/ingest_receipts/ingest-2024-11-10.json which lists batches and counts. If auditors want Splunk/Elastic screenshots, we export saved-query JSON defs and a 2-minute dashboard GIF via the evidence exporter.
rbac_evidence_locations: Canonical artifacts and locations: - RBAC policy export: s3://redwood-config-dumps/rbac/v2/exports/rbac_v2_policy_export_2024-11-01.json - Access review report: gdrive:shared_drives/security-and-compliance/access-reviews/2024-Q4-review.csv - Enforcement logs (authorization decisions): s3://audit-logs/authorization/2024/11/ - Policy-change PRs: github.com/redwood/infra/pulls?query=label:rbac-policy - Live demos: console route /admin/rbac/policies?snapshot=true. For each path, include SHA256 of the exported file and a signed delivery note in the snapshot bundle.
automation_gap_notes: Known automation gaps to disclose to auditors: 1) Some long-tail policy change emails are still recorded only in mail archives (engineering@) not in structured policy-change events; mitigation: manual export script and attachment to snapshot. 2) Staging SIEM ingest uses a different pipeline (legacy lambda) that does not include session_id in a dedicated field; mitigation: mapping table provided and conversion script (scripts/legacy-to-canonical.py). 3) Evidence retention metadata occasionally lacks ingestion timestamps when objects migrated from earlier buckets; mitigation: retention_augment job run to backfill ingest_ts for affected objects.
auditor_qna_script: Use this as a live script during walkthroughs (scripted prompts and suggested talking points): - Q: How do you assert the RBAC policy in effect during the audit window? A: We present the RBAC v2 policy export and a signed manifest plus policy-change events from the audit log showing timeline around the export. - Q: Where are authorization decisions recorded and how are they correlated to user identities? A: Authorization decisions are stored in s3/audit/authorization with user_id and trace_id; we demonstrate correlation via a trace_id example (trace-4f2a) and a console replay. - Q: How do you ensure logs are not tampered with? A: SIEM ingest receipts have cryptographic checksums and S3 Object Lock is enabled for the retention buckets; we also provide a KMS access policy snapshot. - Q: What is your sampling rationale? A: Explain deterministic coverage + stratified random sampling with seed and exact query used. - Q: Any exceptions or compensating controls? A: Be transparent about staged exceptions (legacy pipeline), show remediation schedule and test replays.
evidence_snapshot_instructions: How to build a repeatable snapshot bundle: 1) Run ./scripts/export-rbac.sh --date <YYYY-MM-DD> -> produces rbac_v2_policy_export_<date>.json and signed hash. 2) Run ./scripts/sample-logs.sh --seed <seed> --count 600 -> produces siem_export_sample_<date>.ndjson. 3) Collect access review CSVs and include access-review-2024-Q4.csv. 4) Run ./scripts/package-bundle.sh <bundle-name> which creates s3://redwood-evidence/audit-snapshots/<bundle-name>.zip and posts a delivery note to Jira SEC-4123. 5) Verify bundle signature with ./scripts/verify-bundle.sh and capture output in snapshot_manifest.txt.
common_auditor_findings_and_replies: We often see auditors probe: 'missing ingest timestamps', 'unclear retention justification', 'incomplete correlation ids'. Suggested responses: provide the retention policy doc and show the retention_augment backfill job run log; for correlation ids provide an end-to-end trace example with a user action -> auth decision -> SIEM ingest -> dashboard screenshot; for missing timestamps show the backfill script and commit that added metadata with a timestamp and PR link. Always include JIRA ticket links for outstanding remediations.
next_steps: 1) Run a dry-run with internal audit (target date: 2025-01-19). 2) Patch legacy ingest mapping in SEC-4123 branch and run evidence-collector nightly for 3 days. 3) Create a signed canonical snapshot and get stakeholder approval (Priya). 4) Schedule auditor walkthrough and share bundle two business days prior. 5) Convert this guide into a short runbook and add to Confluence.
notes_to_self: Keep copies of any ad-hoc screenshots in evidence_scratch/ and link to the bundle. If an auditor asks for raw syslogs, be prepared to redact IPs and use redaction-certified utility (scripts/redact-ips.py). Remember to sign every exported artifact and record the verifier output in Jira before the walkthrough.
